overview: Chocolate agar is, quite literally, blood agar that has been deliberately damaged to feed pickier organisms.
genZNote: One shows you hemolysis. One just wants everyone to grow.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: An enriched, non-selective medium made with 5% sheep blood added to a nutrient agar base; supports most organisms and shows hemolysis patterns.
aspects.valueB: Enriched medium made by heating blood agar until red cells lyse, releasing nutrients (hemoglobin-bound iron, NAD) in a usable form.

aspects.label: Preparation
aspects.valueA: Sheep blood is added to cooled (not hot) molten agar base, keeping red cells intact.
aspects.valueB: Blood is added to hot agar base, lysing the cells and giving the medium its characteristic brown 'chocolate' color.

aspects.label: Hemolysis Reading
aspects.valueA: Supports and displays hemolysis patterns: beta (clear), alpha (green), or gamma (none).
aspects.valueB: Cannot be used to assess hemolysis, since red cells are already lysed during preparation.

aspects.label: Target Organisms
aspects.valueA: General-purpose for most bacteria and fungi; used to detect Streptococcus hemolysis patterns.
aspects.valueB: Supports fastidious organisms that need factors released from lysed cells, notably Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria species.

aspects.label: Clinical Use
aspects.valueA: Routine primary plating medium for most clinical specimens.
aspects.valueB: Added alongside blood agar specifically when a fastidious respiratory or genital pathogen is suspected.

aspects.label: Incubation Conditions
aspects.valueA: Standard aerobic or CO2-enriched incubation depending on the suspected organism.
aspects.valueB: Usually incubated in a CO2-enriched atmosphere to support fastidious growth.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Intact red cells allow hemolysis typing.
aspects.valueB: Lysed red cells release growth factors for fastidious organisms but remove the ability to read hemolysis.
